# Immowelt.de Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/immowelt-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/immowelt-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects property listing data from Immowelt.de, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Immowelt.de Real Estate Data](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-immowelt-de-real-estate-properties)
- **Code:** [`immowelt.py`](immowelt.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Property pages](results/properties.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json)

## What it scrapes

- Immowelt property pages for property listing data
- Immowelt property search for finding property listings

## Functions

- `scrape_properties(urls)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape listings data from property pages
- `scrape_search(url, max_scrape_pages=None)` → `List[Dict]`: scrape search pages from XHR call responses

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import immowelt


async def main():
    properties = await immowelt.scrape_properties(
        urls=[
            "https://www.immowelt.de/expose/k2ag632",
            "https://www.immowelt.de/expose/k2bw932",
        ],
    )
    search = await immowelt.scrape_search(
        url="https://www.immowelt.de/classified-search?distributionTypes=Buy&estateTypes=Apartment&locations=AD08DE6345",
        max_scrape_pages=3,
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields of the sample output (top-level keys of the first item):

- [`results/properties.json`](results/properties.json): `brand`, `id`, `sections`, `contactSections`, `tags`
- [`results/search.json`](results/search.json): `brand`, `id`, `status`, `metadata`, `location`, `hardFacts`, `gallery`, `tracking`, `provider`, `cardProvider`, `energyClass`, `mainDescription`, `type`, `url`, `portal`, `rawData`, `tags`, `display`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`immowelt.py`](immowelt.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"DE"`: country of the proxy

## Notes

In the property search scraper, you need to add `location_ids` to the API request body, which represents the search location. To get these ids, follow these steps:  
1. Search for properties in a specific location on immowelt.de  
2. Open developer tools and select the `Network` tab then filter by `Fetch/XHR` requests  
3. Click on the next search page button to load more data  
4. You will see the request made to the search API, which is named `searches`  
5. Grab the `location_ids` from the request `Payload`:

<img src="https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/assets/73492002/e6a80576-c6ed-4e47-9e46-6677522a5809" align="center" height="400" width="600">  
<br/><br/>

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/immowelt-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_properties_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
